answer: An agent market requires each identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can bid on jobs, whether it maps an orchard, updates an atlas, or transcribes a whisper. Bonds cannot back multiple identities at once. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up $100,000 for a month, with financing costs and lost access to that capital. New names are cheap, but every eligible identity requires another bond.
